claims.label: equivalence
claims.mathematical_claim: For r>0, H satisfying r-UUS, and 0<e_a,e_g<=r: H is (e_a,e_g)-uniformly generatable iff C_{e_a,e_g}(H)<infinity.

claims.label: quantitative proof guarantee
claims.mathematical_claim: If C=d<infinity, the sufficient uniform covering-number threshold is d+1; the proof selects a point of the closure outside the union of observed closed e_g-balls.

standing_assumptions.G1: Throughout the paper (X,rho) is a separable metric space and H is a binary hypothesis class, a subset of {0,1}^X. No countability of H or X is imposed unless a particular claim says so.
standing_assumptions.G2: B(x,e) is closed (rho(x,y)<=e). For a set A, B(A,e)={y:inf_{x in A}rho(x,y)<=e}; for infinite A this is an infimum-based neighborhood, not necessarily a union of point-balls. N(e;A,rho) is the least size of a finite e-cover, with centers anywhere in X; it is infinity if no finite cover exists.
standing_assumptions.G3: r-UUS requires every target support nonempty and, for every positive infinite sequence whose range r-covers that support, N(r;its finite prefixes,rho) tends to infinity. It is a covering-stream condition, not merely that supports have infinitely many points. r>0. It implies delta-UUS for 0<delta<r. Unless the claim obtains UUS at every radius, generation scales satisfy 0<e_a,e_g<=r.
standing_assumptions.G4: A generator is a total map G:X*->X. Success on a finite observed prefix means output in the true support and outside its closed e_g-neighborhood, hence distance strictly greater than e_g from each observation. Only observed examples enter the exclusion set; earlier generator outputs do not. Definitions quantify arbitrary positive streams and impose no pairwise separation or no-repetition requirement on them.
standing_assumptions.G6: Uniform generation: exists G and a common natural threshold d*, independent of target and positive stream, such that if a prefix has e_a-covering number at least d*, all outputs from that round onward succeed. Non-uniform: exists one G; for each h there is a threshold d_h, independent of positive stream, with the same guarantee. These notions quantify all positive streams, without requiring support coverage. The threshold is a covering-number threshold, not a number-of-rounds bound.
standing_assumptions.G7: The version space consists of hypotheses containing every observation. The induced closure is the intersection of supports in a nonempty version space, and is bottom for an inconsistent sample. C_{e_a,e_g}(H) is the largest attainable finite-sample e_a-covering number d for a realizable sample whose closure has a finite internal e_g-cover F subset closure. It is infinity for unbounded such d, and zero if there are no witnesses. Internal centers are essential here, unlike N, whose centers may be anywhere in X.
standing_assumptions.G9: The generation results are existence/semantic statements about total maps, with no general computability or finite-query promise. An ERM value oracle tests closure membership on a realizable positive sample by labeling a candidate negative. A separate max-min search oracle, with a fixed default point on empty feasible sets, implements the uniform guarantee with one oracle call per round. It is not reduced to finitely many ERM queries. ERM enumeration search needs exact novelty tests and a supplied candidate sequence meeting the novel closure; density in X alone and separability alone do not ensure this. Such conditional search can fail to terminate on other samples. A terminating fallback/decidable threshold requires further assumptions not adopted. A general finite-ERM implementation remains unresolved by this argument.

comparison: The iff is the source uniform-generation characterization on its intended nonempty, separable metric, r-UUS, positive-scale domain. component_comparison.detail: Same uniform quantifier order and finite internal-cover witness criterion; formal finite-bound predicate is equivalent to C<infinity.

The dimension-bound helper uses D+1 to rule out finite internal covers. scaleClosureGenerator selects a novel common-core point if one exists. The exported iff does not expose a numeric minimal dimension or an exact sample-complexity equality.

strength_assessment.qualification: Nonempty X is explicit in Lean and tacitly needed by the source total-generator convention. Formal conditional generation outside UUS may be vacuous.
strength_assessment.source_implication: The source-domain iff is recovered without strengthening a source hypothesis.

representation_and_access: S1-S8; realizable finite samples and internal centers match. Bottom versus universal core on inconsistent histories is guarded away. There is no numeric dimension-value API.
algorithm_scope: Semantic existence. Native scaleClosureGenerator performs a classical existence test and choice of a fresh core point, with a default output. It matches the source choice-based sufficiency scheme, not Appendix E max-min/finite-ERM execution.

discrepancies.detail: The theorem has a broader domain and scale range; source positive boundaries remain covered.

claims.label: simultaneous separation
claims.mathematical_claim: For every r>0 there are a single class H on ell_2 and a metric rho-prime bi-Lipschitz equivalent to ordinary rho such that H is r-UUS and (e,e)-uniformly generatable under rho for every 0<e<r, but is not (e,e)-non-uniformly generatable under rho-prime for any 0<e<r. The proof verifies r-UUS under both metrics.

claims.label: source metric and supports
claims.mathematical_claim: rho-prime(x,y)=(sum_j delta_j(x_j-y_j)^2)^(1/2), delta_j=1 for odd j and 1/4 for even j; rho/2<=rho-prime<=rho. alpha_m=2^(3-m)r, a_{m,k}=alpha_m e_k; A_{m,I}={a_{m,2^n(2k+1)}:k in I,n>=0}. Supports are {0} union union_{m>=1} A_{m,I_m} for an independent infinite positive-index set I_m in each layer.

standing_assumptions.G1: Throughout the paper (X,rho) is a separable metric space and H is a binary hypothesis class, a subset of {0,1}^X. No countability of H or X is imposed unless a particular claim says so.
standing_assumptions.G2: B(x,e) is closed (rho(x,y)<=e). For a set A, B(A,e)={y:inf_{x in A}rho(x,y)<=e}; for infinite A this is an infimum-based neighborhood, not necessarily a union of point-balls. N(e;A,rho) is the least size of a finite e-cover, with centers anywhere in X; it is infinity if no finite cover exists.
standing_assumptions.G3: r-UUS requires every target support nonempty and, for every positive infinite sequence whose range r-covers that support, N(r;its finite prefixes,rho) tends to infinity. It is a covering-stream condition, not merely that supports have infinitely many points. r>0. It implies delta-UUS for 0<delta<r. Unless the claim obtains UUS at every radius, generation scales satisfy 0<e_a,e_g<=r.
standing_assumptions.G4: A generator is a total map G:X*->X. Success on a finite observed prefix means output in the true support and outside its closed e_g-neighborhood, hence distance strictly greater than e_g from each observation. Only observed examples enter the exclusion set; earlier generator outputs do not. Definitions quantify arbitrary positive streams and impose no pairwise separation or no-repetition requirement on them.
standing_assumptions.G6: Uniform generation: exists G and a common natural threshold d*, independent of target and positive stream, such that if a prefix has e_a-covering number at least d*, all outputs from that round onward succeed. Non-uniform: exists one G; for each h there is a threshold d_h, independent of positive stream, with the same guarantee. These notions quantify all positive streams, without requiring support coverage. The threshold is a covering-number threshold, not a number-of-rounds bound.
standing_assumptions.G8: Doubling means one uniform bound M on the number of radius-s/2 balls covering any radius-s ball, for every center and s>0. In a doubling space r-UUS for one r>0 implies UUS at all positive radii. Equivalent metrics means bi-Lipschitz: c rho_1 <= rho_2 <= C rho_1 for constants 0<c<=C<infinity, rather than merely equal topology.

comparison: The same class and an actual MetricSpace structure are chosen before every epsilon; all e in (0,r) have the source ordinary-metric uniform/weighted-metric non-uniform separation. Both r-UUS properties are explicit conjuncts, so no support qualification is omitted.

claims.label: source construction

comparison: The two-hypothesis Hilbert obstruction is fully represented at every strictly reversed positive scale pair, with r-UUS and failure of non-uniform generation. Set.ncard H=2 expresses exact two-element cardinality under the trusted standard semantics.

component_comparison.detail: For r>0 and 0<e_a<e_g<=r there exists H with exactly two languages, r-UUS, and not non-uniformly generatable.

Native small points use a e_{3(k+1)}; the two remote families use coordinates 3(k+1)+1 and 3(k+1)+2 with amplitude 2r. Boolean indexing selects the two residue classes. This is the paper two-support geometry with positive indices.
